easy.def: The huge place beyond Earth.
examples: Astronauts go to space.
Stars are in space.
A rocket flies into space.

more.def: The huge, dark area beyond Earth where the stars and planets are.
examples: Astronauts travel to space in rockets.
Stars twinkle across space.
The telescope looks deep into space.

easy.def: Room for something.
examples: There is space for one more.
Save me a space.
The closet has little space.

more.def: An empty area or room where something can go.
examples: We found a space for the couch.
There was no space left in the car.
She left a space between the words.

easy.def: Extra.
examples: I have a spare key.
We have a spare tire.
Take a spare pencil.

more.def: Kept in case it is needed; extra.
examples: I keep a spare key under the mat.
The car has a spare tire.
Bring a spare pencil to the test.

easy.def: To save from harm.
examples: Spare the flowers.
The storm spared our house.
He spared the bug.

more.def: To keep someone or something from being hurt.
examples: The flood spared the old barn.
She spared the tiny spider and put it outside.
The king spared the prisoner.

easy.def: A tiny bit of fire that flies up.
examples: A spark flew from the fire.
The campfire made a spark.
I saw a spark.

more.def: A tiny, bright bit of fire that flies off something that is burning or rubbed.
examples: A spark flew from the campfire.
The wires gave off a spark.
The flint made a spark when he struck it.

easy.def: To say words out loud.
examples: Speak slowly.
He spoke to me.
The baby cannot speak yet.

more.def: To say words out loud, or to be able to use a language.
examples: Please speak clearly so the whole class can hear you.
My neighbor speaks three languages.
The principal spoke to the school about the field trip.

easy.def: A person who gives a talk.
examples: The speaker was funny.
A guest speaker came.
The speaker told a story.

more.def: A person who talks to a group of people.
examples: The guest speaker told us about her trip.
The speaker was funny and clear.
Each speaker had five minutes.

easy.def: A box that gives out sound.
examples: The speaker is loud.
Turn up the speaker.
The speaker plays music.

more.def: The part of a radio or computer that gives out sound.
examples: The speaker is too loud.
I plugged the speaker into the computer.
Music came from the small speaker.

easy.def: A long pole with a sharp point.
examples: The hunter held a spear.
The spear is long.
The museum has an old spear.

more.def: A long pole with a sharp point that was used long ago for hunting.
examples: The museum has an ancient spear.
The hunter in the story carried a spear.
The spear was made of wood and stone.

easy.def: Different and better than usual.
examples: Today is a special day.
Grandma made a special cake.
You are special to me.

more.def: Better, different or more important than usual.
examples: We eat a special meal on the last day of school.
The museum has a special show about space.
The toy was special because my grandpa made it.

easy.def: Meant for one job.
examples: Firefighters wear special coats.
The cat has a special bed.
This special paper is for painting.

more.def: Made or meant for one particular use or person.
examples: Astronauts wear special suits in space.
The shop sells special shoes for running.
The bus has a special seat for people who need help.

easy.def: A person who knows a lot about one subject.
examples: The doctor is a specialist.
A specialist helped.
She is a heart specialist.

more.def: A person who has special training and knows a lot about one thing.
examples: The doctor is a heart specialist.
A specialist in birds visited our class.
The specialist fixed the machine.

easy.def: For a certain purpose.
examples: The cake was specially made.
This is specially for you.
The room was specially built.

more.def: In a way that is meant for one purpose or person.
examples: The cake was specially made for her birthday.
This card is specially for you.
The shoes were specially made for dancing.

easy.def: A kind of animal or plant.
examples: A lion is a species of cat.
This species is rare.
There are many species of birds.

more.def: A group of animals or plants that are alike and can have young together.
examples: The panda is an endangered species.
This rare species lives only on one island.
Scientists have found thousands of new species.

easy.def: Exact and clear.
examples: Be specific about what you want.
I need a specific book.
She gave a specific answer.

more.def: Clear and exact, about one particular thing and not just any.
examples: Please give a specific time for the party.
I need a specific book for my report.
The teacher asked for specific details in the story.

easy.def: Talking.
examples: Speech lets us share ideas.
Her speech is clear.
Birds do not have speech.

more.def: The ability to speak, or the way a person talks.
examples: Speech lets people share ideas.
The baby's speech improved.
His speech was clear and slow.

easy.def: A talk given to a group.
examples: The mayor gave a speech.
I gave a speech in class.
Her speech was short.

more.def: A talk that someone gives to a group of people.
examples: The principal gave a speech at assembly.
I practiced my speech in front of the mirror.
The mayor's speech lasted ten minutes.

easy.def: How fast something goes.
examples: The car has great speed.
A cheetah has great speed.
Speed matters in a race.

more.def: How fast something moves.
examples: The cheetah is known for its speed.
The train slowed its speed near the station.
Wind speed can change quickly.

easy.def: To go very fast.
examples: The car sped by.
We speed down the hill.
The train speeds along.

more.def: To move very fast.
examples: The race car sped around the track.
We sped down the hill on our sleds.
The train speeds across the country.

easy.def: To say or write the letters of a word.
examples: Spell your name.
I can spell cat.
She spelled the word.

more.def: To name or write the letters of a word in order.
examples: Can you spell your last name?
She spelled the word correctly.
We practice how to spell new words each week.

easy.def: Magic words in stories.
examples: The witch cast a spell.
The wizard said a spell.
The spell broke.

more.def: Magic words that make something happen in stories.
examples: The wizard cast a spell on the castle.
The witch said a spell and the frog turned into a prince.
The spell broke at midnight.

easy.def: To use money to buy things.
examples: I spend my coins on stickers.
I spent a dollar on a toy.
He spent his allowance on a book.

more.def: To pay money for things.
examples: She spent all her birthday money on art supplies.
Families spend a lot on food each week.
The town spent money fixing the old bridge.

easy.def: To use time doing something.
examples: We spent the day at the beach.
She spends time with her dog.
I spend my mornings at school.

more.def: To pass time doing something or being somewhere.
examples: We spent the whole summer at my grandparents' farm.
He spends an hour each night reading.
The owl spends the daytime sleeping in a hollow tree.

easy.def: A small animal with eight legs that makes a web.
examples: A spider made a web.
The spider has eight legs.
I saw a spider.

more.def: A small creature with eight legs that spins webs to catch insects.
examples: A spider spun a web between the branches.
Spiders have eight legs.
The spider waited in its web for a fly.

easy.def: A long, sharp point.
examples: The fence has spikes.
The cactus has spikes.
The spike is sharp.

more.def: A thin piece of metal or wood with a sharp point.
examples: The fence had metal spikes on top.
The runner's shoes had spikes.
A spike stuck out of the board.

easy.def: To let something run out by accident.
examples: Do not spill the milk.
I spilled my juice.
She spilled the paint.

more.def: To let a liquid or a powder run out of its container by accident.
examples: I spilled my juice on the table.
Be careful not to spill the paint.
She spilled sugar all over the floor.

easy.def: To turn around and around fast.
examples: The top will spin.
I spin in a circle.
The wheel spun.

more.def: To turn around and around quickly, or to make something do this.
examples: The ice skater spun on one foot.
The washing machine spins the clothes dry.
The dancers spun in a circle.

easy.def: The part of a person that feels and thinks.
examples: She has a happy spirit.
The team had spirit.
He has a kind spirit.

more.def: The part of a person that is not the body, which feels and thinks.
examples: She has a cheerful spirit.
The team showed great spirit.
The spirit of the holiday is giving.

easy.def: A ghost or make-believe being.
examples: The spirit lived in the woods.
The story has a friendly spirit.
The spirit of the forest.

more.def: A make-believe being, such as a ghost.
examples: The spirit of the old house moved the curtains.
In the legend, a spirit lived in the lake.
The story has a kind spirit that helps a lost child.

easy.def: Having to do with the soul or religion.
examples: Prayer is spiritual.
She has spiritual beliefs.
The spiritual leader spoke.

more.def: Having to do with the soul or with religion, not with things you can touch.
examples: Prayer is a spiritual practice.
The spiritual leader gave a talk.
She finds peace in her spiritual life.

easy.def: To push water or food out from your mouth.
examples: Do not spit.
The baby spit out the peas.
The camel spat.

more.def: To force something out of your mouth.
examples: He spit out a seed from the watermelon.
The llama spat grass at the zookeeper.
The cat spit when it got scared.

easy.def: A wish to hurt someone.
examples: He broke it out of spite.
She acted in spite.
Spite is mean.

more.def: A mean wish to hurt or upset someone.
examples: He broke the toy out of spite.
She told the secret in spite.
Acting out of spite is unkind.

easy.def: To make water fly up.
examples: I splash in the puddle.
The kids splashed in the pool.
The fish splashed.

more.def: To make water fly about with a sudden movement.
examples: I splashed in the puddle with my boots.
The waves splashed against the rocks.
The ducks splashed in the pond.

easy.def: The sound or sight of water flying up.
examples: I heard a splash.
The splash got me wet.
The frog jumped with a splash.

more.def: A burst of water thrown up, or the sound it makes.
examples: The frog jumped into the pond with a splash.
I heard a splash in the lake.
The splash soaked my shirt.

easy.def: Very fine and grand.
examples: We had a splendid day.
The palace was splendid.
What a splendid idea!

more.def: Very beautiful or impressive.
examples: The palace looked splendid in the sunlight.
We had a splendid time at the fair.
The band gave a splendid show.

easy.def: To break into parts.
examples: The log split.
We split the pizza.
The ice split.

more.def: To break or divide into parts.
examples: The log split in two.
We split the pizza between us.
The ice began to split in the spring.

easy.def: A long crack or tear.
examples: There is a split in my pants.
The wood has a split.
The split in the board is long.

more.def: A long crack or opening where something has divided.
examples: There is a split in the old log.
A split in the seam let the stuffing out.
The ice had a long split down the middle.

easy.def: To make something bad or not good.
examples: Rain will spoil our picnic.
The milk will spoil.
Do not spoil the surprise.

more.def: To ruin something, or to go bad and become unfit to eat.
examples: The rain spoiled our picnic.
Milk can spoil if it is not kept cold.
He spoiled the surprise by telling us.

related.def: Something that tells how a story ends before you read it.

easy.def: A soft thing that soaks up water.
examples: I wash with a sponge.
The sponge is wet.
She squeezed the sponge.

more.def: A soft, light material full of holes that soaks up water, used for washing.
examples: I wiped the table with a sponge.
She squeezed the sponge over the sink.
A sponge soaks up a lot of water.

easy.def: A person or business that pays for something.
examples: A store was the sponsor.
The sponsor paid for the shirts.
We thanked the sponsor.

more.def: A person or company that pays for a team or event.
examples: A local store was the team's sponsor.
The sponsor paid for our new shirts.
We thanked the sponsor of the fair.

easy.def: A tool for eating soup or cereal.
examples: I eat soup with a spoon.
The spoon is silver.
Put a spoon in the bowl.

more.def: A tool with a small bowl on a handle, used for eating, stirring or serving.
examples: I ate my cereal with a spoon.
Mom stirred the soup with a wooden spoon.
She put a spoon of sugar in her tea.

easy.def: A game that uses your body.
examples: Soccer is my favorite sport.
Swimming is a sport.
He plays a sport.

more.def: A game or activity in which people use their bodies and often compete.
examples: Soccer is the most popular sport in the world.
Swimming is her favorite sport.
He plays a different sport every season.

easy.def: A small mark.
examples: There is a spot on my shirt.
A ladybug has black spots.
A leopard has spots.

more.def: A small mark or round area that is different from what is around it.
examples: A ladybug has black spots on its red back.
There is a spot of paint on the floor.
A dog with brown spots ran by.

easy.def: A place.
examples: This is a good spot for a picnic.
I found a quiet spot.
Save my spot.

more.def: A particular place.
examples: We found a shady spot for the picnic.
This is my favorite fishing spot.
Save me a spot in line.

easy.def: To see something.
examples: I spot a bird.
She spotted a deer.
Can you spot the cat?

more.def: To notice or see something that is hard to find.
examples: I spotted a deer at the edge of the woods.
Can you spot the hidden picture?
She spotted her friend in the crowd.

easy.def: To sit or lie with your arms and legs spread out.
examples: The cat sprawled on the rug.
He sprawled on the couch.
I sprawled on the grass.

more.def: To lie or sit with your body stretched out in a lazy way.
examples: The cat sprawled on the warm rug.
He sprawled on the couch after dinner.
I sprawled on the grass and watched the clouds.

easy.def: To send out tiny drops of water.
examples: I spray the plants.
She sprayed water on the flowers.
The hose sprays.

more.def: To send out liquid in a fine mist of tiny drops.
examples: I sprayed water on the plants.
The whale sprayed water from its blowhole.
He sprayed the car with a hose.

easy.def: Tiny drops of water in the air.
examples: The spray of the waves was cold.
The spray from the hose was cool.
A spray of water hit me.

more.def: A mist of tiny drops of liquid, or a can that makes one.
examples: The spray from the waves cooled us off.
A spray of water from the fountain wet my shoes.
The bug spray smelled strong.

easy.def: To put on in a thin layer.
examples: Spread jam on the bread.
He spread butter.
She spread paint on the paper.

more.def: To cover a surface with a thin layer of something.
examples: Spread jam on your toast.
She spread paint across the paper.
Dad spread butter on the corn.

easy.def: To get bigger or reach more places.
examples: The news spread.
The fire spread.
The flowers spread across the field.

more.def: To reach or cover more space.
examples: The news spread fast.
Weeds spread across the garden.
The flowers spread across the hillside.

easy.def: The season after winter.
examples: Flowers bloom in spring.
Spring is warm.
Birds sing in spring.

more.def: The season between winter and summer, when plants begin to grow.
examples: Flowers bloom in the spring.
Spring brings warmer days and longer light.
We plant our garden in the spring.

easy.def: A coil of metal that bounces back.
examples: The toy has a spring.
The bed has springs.
A spring makes it bounce.

more.def: A twisty piece of metal that returns to its shape after it is pressed or pulled.
examples: The toy jumped on a spring.
The old mattress had a broken spring.
A spring inside the pen makes it click.

easy.def: To jump suddenly.
examples: The cat sprang onto the couch.
He springs up.
The frog sprang away.

more.def: To jump or move suddenly and quickly.
examples: The cat sprang onto the table.
The runner sprang from the starting line.
The frog sprang into the pond.

easy.def: A person who secretly gets information.
examples: The spy listened.
The spy wore a hat.
A spy hides.

more.def: A person who secretly watches others to get information.
examples: The spy hid behind the curtain.
In the story, a spy sent secret messages.
The spy wore a hat to hide his face.

easy.def: To see.
examples: I spy a bird.
She spied a frog.
He spies the cat.

more.def: To catch sight of something.
examples: I spy a bird in the tree.
She spied a frog by the pond.
He spied his friend in the crowd.
